To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an efficient and highly selective synthesis of pyrimidones via [Cp*CO] catalyzed amidation.

we have developed a highly efficient, selective and practical method for the synthesis of enamides, pyrimidones and pyrazoles via C-H amidations of N-methoxyl acrylamides, dioxazolone and pyrazole-5-carboxamides, respectively.

a highly efficient and selective method has been developed for C–H amidation of N -methoxy acrylamide and N -methoxy aryl amide with dioxazolidone to afford the corresponding enamides and pyrazolones, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new synthetic methods for the synthesis of enamides.
the development of highly efficient, selective and atom-economical catalytic methods for the synthesis of enamides, pyrimidones and related compounds.
the development of a highly efficient and selective method for the synthesis of enamides, pyrimidones and pyrimidinones via C-H amidations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the C-H amidation reaction of N-methoxycarboxamides is a highly efficient and selective method for the synthesis of enamides, and the pyrimidone product can be obtained in a highly efficient and highly selective manner.
the [Cp* CoIII] catalytic system has been demonstrated to be a versatile platform for the selective synthesis of a variety of nitrogen-containing heterocycles via C-H amidations.
the [Cp*COIII]-catalyzed C-H amidation reaction has been successfully applied to the selective synthesis of enamines, enamides, and pyrimidone derivatives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the [Cp* CoIII] catalyst can selectively catalyze a series of C-H amidation reactions of olefinic C-H bonds, and also the aryl C-H bond.
the [Cp* CoIII] catalyst is able to catalyze a series of C-H amidation reactions of N-methoxycarbamate derivatives.
a single [Cp*COIII] catalyst can be used to catalyze three different C-H bond activation reactions to form three different classes of products.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the [Cp*CO(iii)] catalyst is able to activate both the olefin and the aryl C-H bond, which enables the C-H bond amidation of olefins and aryl C(sp(2))-H bonds with dioxazoles.
the C(sp(2))-H activation of N-methoxylated substrates is a general strategy for C-H functionalization.
the Cp*Co(iii) catalysis enables the selective synthesis of enamines and pyrimidines from C-H amidation, which is a new strategy for the synthesis of these compounds.
